content.rationale: The decision is a page composition whose refs are code (media/webview.html, src/webview/main.ts), and the prerequisites it mounts are code artefacts too — the renderer (rtlotqvy), the search page module (uryrrttr), the interaction and keyboard state (noplrntp), the presentation (yruxqknp), the page interface (ympqvvwr), the graph model and order (qmsmvrnr), the detail-section behaviour (vqwoptmu, yrtrqutm, qwzwpxws, rmovtvkt), the toolbar action (mspmqvuk) and the page regions (zrqxuzzy) — so the code-to-code cell applies and the check is a runnable test. The composition test parses the real media/webview.html, adopts its body into jsdom, loads the source entry src/webview/main.ts into it and posts graphs across the page's message seam; it then drives the composed page as a user does: it reads the regions the page interface names, counts the node boxes and routed edges the renderer draws into the canvas layers, clicks a node and reads the detail region back, posts a warning and reads the banner, presses the toolbar's fit action and reads the viewport transform, presses `/` and reads a focused field, types a query and reads the match class on exactly the matching boxes, presses Enter and reads the newly selected box and its detail, presses Esc and reads the field, the marks and the selection gone, and posts a reload containing a node the query newly matches and reads the active query, the re-applied marks and the kept selection (including that only one search is attached). The detail test drives the same composed page for the detail panel it renders (vqwoptmu, yrtrqutm, qwzwpxws, rmovtvkt). The check names no composition function, field or event wiring the record does not fix: it finds the regions and the drawn identity through the page interface's exported selectors and attributes, the match emphasis through the search module's exported class, and the query field as the input the page puts over the canvas, so any page that mounts these modules and shows the committed behaviour passes. The refine adds two prerequisites whose content is words rather than an artefact — activating an id the panel lists selects the node it names and shows its detail as clicking its box does (kwxutvpw), and an id listed from an edge whose other end names no node document is listed but inert (rusopkql) — so those two edges sit in the natural-to-code (fidelity) cell, and the same runnable test carries them: the prose names observables, so fidelity can be applied by running the composed page instead of reading it, in both directions. The check reads every id a relationship section lists and activates it as a user does — a primary pointer pressed and released on the entry, then the compatibility click the browser adds and addresses to the element that captured the pointer if one holds it for that pointer and otherwise to the nearest common inclusive ancestor of the press and the release, and Enter and Space on the element around the entry that takes the keyboard focus — and requires the page to land on exactly the selection and the detail region a click on the node's own box gives, so the page enforces nothing less than the prose claims (kwxutvpw); and it requires an id whose edge names no node document to stay listed while the same pointer and key activation leave the selection and the detail region as they were, so the page adds nothing the prose does not allow and an inert entry never becomes a selection (rusopkql). Neither direction fixes a tag, a class, an attribute, a handler or a controller call: the id is found as the element that shows it inside the section its label names, the control as the element around it that takes the focus, and the observables read back are the page interface's own selection emphasis and the detail region the panel renders. The key press is applied the way a browser applies it, so the two inputs stay told apart: a native control the browser itself activates on a keypress — a button, a link with an href, a form button, a summary — is given the click the browser would fire, because jsdom runs none of that activation, while every other element is left to activate itself on the keydown, since for a span or a div that keyboard behaviour is the page's own obligation and a fallback click would hide a missing key handler. An entry that answered no key at all, or answered Enter and not Space, therefore fails the check even though the pointer gesture could carry it. The click a press and release ends in is addressed as a browser addresses it and not handed to the entry: jsdom runs no pointer capture, so the check keeps the browser's bookkeeping for it, and an entry the page can only reach by a click dispatched at it by hand — one sitting inside the element the page captures the pointer on, where a browser would address the click to the capturing element — is not activated by the check. The refine also retracts the composition's sentence that the entries add no appearance of their own, and adds eight prerequisites whose content is words over the mark the entries now carry: a listed id is presented as a visible link (mwwxxzyk), and that link takes the link colour role (tvoouwkn), the pointer cursor (rqrlnzny), the hover underline (qnmuwwvw) and the accent focus outline while it has the focus (vvzptxmz), while an entry whose id names no node document is drawn in the muted secondary role (mplxzxnm) and takes no pointer cursor, no hover underline and no focus outline (kpkstnps), and the markup and the stylesheet meet on one fixed vocabulary of two class names — detail__entry for the entry that names a node document and detail__entry--inert for the entry that names none, exactly one of the two on any listed entry and nothing beside it — the recorded pair is the whole vocabulary, so no third class, no further modifier on either name and no second entry name is on an entry (sqwusxql). Those eight edges are words over an artefact, so they sit in the natural-to-code (fidelity) cell and the same runnable test carries them: the composed page is run and the entries its panel renders are read back by the class each one carries, so the page enforces the mapping in both directions — every id a relationship section lists that names a node document carries detail__entry and every listed id that names none carries detail__entry--inert, with no listed entry left unclassified and none carrying both, and each entry's class list read whole rather than filtered down to the two recorded names: the element of the entry that shows the id carries its case's name alone, and no element of the entry spells a further name out of the two, so a third class or a further modifier added beside the case class is read as the extra name it is and the two recorded names are the whole of what an entry is marked with — and the declarations those classes select, the colour roles, the cursor, the hover rule, the focus outline and the muted role, are left to the check of the stylesheet that writes them, so this one neither restates them nor judges them. The check reads the two names from the record and not from the implementation, and names no element, selector or declaration: the class is read from the element that shows the id and the wrappers around it that show nothing else, so any page that marks its listed entries with the recorded vocabulary passes, whatever element of the entry carries it. The refine also adds two prerequisites whose content is words over the ref paths the Content section shows — a Content ref path is a control that opens that repo-relative file in the editor, activated by a pointer click or by Enter or Space while it has the focus (rptlovpt), and a ref-path entry carries detail__ref as its whole class, the one name the stylesheet's rules select (ppkkmxxu) — so those two edges sit in the natural-to-code (fidelity) cell, and the same two runnable tests carry them, because the composed page can be run rather than read and the prose names its observables: each direction is checked on the page the tests drive, and neither clause fixes a message name, a field name, a tag, a handler, a host-side resolution or failure rule, or a declaration. (a) The paths keep their place: the Content section still shows the content type and every path of a content.ref list in one monospaced block (qwzwpxws), and each of those paths is shown in that block as an entry of its own — the element that holds that path and nothing else, so the type and the list's other paths are not part of it — instead of as bare text in a block that holds them all, which both tests read off the composed page. (b) The entry's mark (ppkkmxxu): the class list of the element that shows the path is read whole and is detail__ref alone, and across the run of elements that hold that path no name is spelled out of it — no modifier on it and no second ref-path name — and neither of the two listed-entry names (detail__entry, detail__entry--inert) reaches a ref path, so the mark is that one name and nothing beside it; the mark is read from the element that shows the path, so any page that keeps the block and marks each path inside it passes, whatever element of the entry carries the name. (c) The activation and its request (rptlovpt): the entry is a control the keyboard can reach, and activating it posts, through the seam the page already declares, the page's request for that repo-relative path. The composition test drives the composed page the way a user does — the path activated by a pointer press and release, whose compatibility click is addressed where a browser addresses it, and, on the focused entry, by Enter and by Space — and reads the request off the page-to-host channel as one message that carries that path as a value of its own, naming neither the node nor the list's other path; where a native control is what the browser itself activates on a keypress it is given the click the browser would fire, and every other element is left to activate itself on the keydown, so an entry that answers no key, or Enter and not Space, fails the check although the pointer press and release could carry it. The activation is the ref path's own: the selection and the detail region the page shows stay as they were, because a path opens a file rather than selecting a node, and kwxutvpw's activation stays the listed ids'. How the host resolves and opens the path is the extension shell's own gate, and the declarations the detail__ref rules carry are the stylesheet's, so this one reads neither; the double-click on a node's box that opens its document (trxzsqpv) is left as it is and is not re-triggered by a ref path. The refine also gives the composition an edge to the centring rule the viewer already keeps (wzsxvmvw): a listed entry's activation must ask the interaction to bring the node that activation selects into view, so the viewport comes to rest where that rule puts it. That standard is a structured artefact — a fixed set of requirement sentences over one axis-and-limit vocabulary — and the subject is code, so the edge sits in the structured-to-code (conformance) cell, and the same runnable test carries it clause by clause: the composed page is run and the viewport it leaves after an activation is read against each clause the sentences state, with nothing they do not state demanded and none of their terms re-decided here. The clause reads the resting viewport per axis from the layout the page draws and the canvas's own size. On an axis the drawn graph fits within the canvas, the centre of the node the activation selected comes to the canvas centre, the margin left at the graph's edge is permitted and the pan limits the page records do not hold the move back; the case is driven at a framing where those limits would have stopped a pan short of that place, so a centring clamped like a pan and a centring that takes the margin are told apart. On an axis the drawn graph overflows, the move is held at the pan limit the page's own pan stops at, read back by panning at the zoom in hand instead of being restated, so the graph keeps covering the canvas and the node is not centred there; that is driven once with the graph overflowing one axis while the other fits and once with it overflowing both, so the two axes are held independently. The near edge that clause reads is the drawn one: the drawn graph spans from the surface origin to the layout's bounds size (rtlotqvy), so an axis the activation holds at the pan limit is read as the resting pan itself, which is where the drawn graph's near edge lies, and not as the pan plus the layout's bounds origin — a reading in the layout's own coordinates, which is the drawn edge only where that origin is zero. The clause is therefore also driven where the origin is not zero, on both axes, so that the frame the renderer draws and the frame the layout states are not the same frame: the posted graph holds a node whose prerequisite names no node document, whose stub stands above a layer-0 box so the layout's bounds start above the boxes, and a node with no prerequisites and no evaluations, which the check drags left of column 0 by the pointer gesture the interaction owns (spllzqlw), so the layout's bounds start left of the boxes, only its own box moving and no route being re-routed; the case refuses itself unless both origins are negative on the graph the page holds, read from the layout module's geometry for the graph the page draws, so a case driven at a zero origin is not credited with having checked the drawn frame. Where the box the drag moved came to rest is read off the page through the origin the page drew the boxes it did not move at — the layout module's place for such a box less the place the page drew it at, which every one of them must answer alike, since the drawing is the layout less one origin and not a frame of its own — so the drop is where the reader put the box and the layout module is given it as the dragged position, and no threshold, rounding or grip offset of the drag is restated here. The drawing is then read the way a reader sees it: every drawn box's own offset plus every translation between it and the node layer added up, required to be the layout's box less the layout's bounds origin, inside a node layer the width of the drawn graph, so the drawing and the viewport the activation writes are held to share the one origin the surface carries (rtlotqvy, noplrntp) instead of each keeping a frame of its own. On that page the centring clause is read in the drawn frame: on a fitted axis the selected node's drawn centre — its layout centre less that origin — comes to the canvas centre, and on an overflowing axis the move is held where the page's own pan stops, with the near edge read as the resting pan; the pan is read off the surface transform at the precision the page spells it out to at the zoom such a case reaches, which is a hundredth of a pixel against a frame difference of hundreds, so a page that kept the layout's own coordinates is told apart by the origin and not by the last digit. The zoom is the one the activation started at, and the selection and the detail region are exactly what the activation already produces (kwxutvpw), since centring is a viewport move and nothing else; an activation of an id whose edge names no node document leaves the viewport where it was (rusopkql). What that clause deliberately does not fix: no member of the composition's internals, no message, no scroll amount, no duration, no easing and no smoothness — it reads the viewport the page comes to rest at, waiting for the surface transform to stop changing so that a move written in the event and one written a frame later are read alike, and it names no transform spelling beyond the one surface the composition already writes and the toolbar's fit clause above already reads. Nor does it judge how the page reaches that move: a page that centres through the focus arrival the interaction already offers is not told apart from one that asks the request the page interface declares, and this edge does not need to tell them apart, because the rule states that both triggers produce one and the same move and leaves whether an activation moves focus to kwxutvpw and the keyboard decisions it cites. A page that reaches that move through a focus arrival can therefore be rejected for the side effect the arrival carries — the focus it moves and the emphasis and keyboard state that follow it — rather than by this clause, which reads only where the viewport comes to rest. The clause also reads the viewport after the selections that are the composition's own ask inventory and nothing else — a pointer click on a node's own box and a ref path's activation, each driven from a view parked where the centring of the node in hand would change it — and requires it to be exactly what it was, so a page that recentres on every selection change, or on a ref path's activation, is read as the move it makes; and there an activation that asks for an id no node document names and one that asks nothing at all are the same reading, because neither moves the viewport and the seam the page declares cannot tell them apart. No coordinate, limit, zoom or framing value is baked into the clause: each is read from what the page draws and from the page's own pans. The clause is driven in every one of the panel's four relationship sections — depends_on, evaluates, dependents and evaluators — and not in depends_on alone, because a listed entry's activation is the activation of the entry the reader activated: a page that asks for the centring only when the id it activates sits among the selected node's prerequisites, and never when it sits among the nodes it evaluates, the nodes that depend on it or the evaluations that name it, asks for the move on one of the four kinds of listed entry the rule states and on none of the other three, and a per-section drive is what tells that page from the composition the decision records. Each of the four sections is populated by the edge that makes it — the selected node's own prerequisite, the node an evaluation evaluates, a node that depends on the selected one, an evaluation that evaluates the selected one — and every id the clause activates names a node document of the posted graph, so each case activates an activatable entry and not an inert one (rusopkql). No single node of a deccy graph lists an entry in all four sections at once: an evaluates entry is an evaluation's, and an evaluation is never another node's prerequisite — a decision's depends_on targets are decisions, and so are an evaluation's — so no evaluation has a dependent; the clause therefore selects, per section, the node the graph honestly gives that section and reads the same terms there, instead of inventing a node that lists all four. The section by regime pairs driven: a framing the drawn graph fits on both axes, for each of the four sections and for each of the three activation inputs (a pointer press and release, Enter, and Space); and, for the three sections other than depends_on, a framing that overflows one axis while the other fits and a framing that overflows both axes — the depends_on pairs of the two overflowing framings are driven beside it, so both ways the axes are held independently are read, and every case is refused when the parked view already rests where the centring belongs. The refine also adds an edge to the selection the search's key presses make (uowtmmqw): that standard is a structured artefact — a fixed set of requirement sentences over the one centring move and the terms the viewport record already carries — and the subject is code, so the edge sits in the structured-to-code (conformance) cell, and the same runnable test carries it clause by clause, with nothing the sentences do not state demanded and none of their terms re-decided here. What the composition now records is where the ask sits: the search module is what asks the interaction for the centring move (uryrrttr), the composition mounts that module and gains no ask of its own for it, and the composition's own ask inventory stays the activation's (wzsxvmvw, kwxutvpw) — which is what the no-move clause above reads. The check reads the new edge on the composed page rather than in its wiring: the field the page puts over the canvas is opened and a query typed, the view is parked where the centring of a node would change it, and the node the key press selects is read off the page interface's own selection emphasis — the direction the walk takes, the set it walks and the node it lands on being the recorded search's (yqwsztww) and never predicted here. The viewport is then required to come to rest where the one centring move puts that node, read per axis with the terms the activation clause above reads — the fitted-axis centre with the margin the recorded pan limit must not hold back, the pan limit where a drawn axis overflows, and the drawn frame where the layout's origin is not zero — at the zoom the key press found and with the zoom left where it was, so the added trigger is what is read and no term of the move is restated. The node centred is the node the selection identifies and no other, so a page that centres on a node it did not select is read as the different move it makes. The drawn boxes are read before and after the key press and required to be the same, and the selection and the detail region stay what the selection already gives, because the move the rule adds is a viewport move and nothing else. Both key presses are driven, since the rule's trigger is the selection either of them makes and the recorded search gives them opposite directions through one marked set: the two land on different marked nodes of the graph the case posts, so a page that answers one of them and not the other is read as the partial move it makes. Where the key presses make no selection — a query that marks no node of the posted graph — the viewport is required to be exactly what it was, so a page that centres on the key press rather than on the selection it makes is read as the move it makes. Nothing the sentences leave to other decisions is re-decided: which key presses act, in which context, over which set they walk, in which direction, order and wrap are yqwsztww's as recorded, which nodes count as marked and what the same key press does outside the search field stay with the decisions yqwsztww names, and whether a selection carries focus onto the node is not assumed, so a page that reaches the move through the focus arrival the interaction already offers is not told apart from one that asks the request the page interface declares — the rule holds both to be one and the same move, and this clause reads only where the viewport comes to rest, waiting for the surface transform to stop changing so that a move written in the event and one written a frame later are read alike. The clause fixes no member of the composition's internals, no message of the page's seam, no scroll amount, no duration, no easing and no smoothness, and it names no transform spelling beyond the surface the toolbar's fit clause already reads. The refine also fixes the order the ask keeps against the selection it accompanies, and it fixes the composition's ask inventory where it is not the activation's. The order is read on the page as composed, at the one moment the page makes both the selection and the ask visible: the page announces each selection it makes through its seam (srlrwowp, ympqvvwr), and the check reads the surface transform inside that announcement. Every viewport so read is required to be the viewport the key press found, so a page that writes the centring before the selection it follows — or that answers the press with a move and no selection — is read as the different order it keeps; and the node the viewport comes to rest centred on afterwards is required to be the node the report names and the node the page emphasises as selected, so a page that centres on a node its own report does not identify is read as the different move it makes. The report is read as the composition's own announcement and no moment is fixed for it beyond the press it answers, and the clause predicts which node neither key press lands on (yqwsztww). Because a page's input queue defers work only while the page presents a load in flight, and the composed page presents no load between the graph it holds and the graph that replaces it, this clause reads the order that queue exists to keep — the ask behind the selection, at the selection's own report — and does not read a deferral: an ask forwarded outside that queue keeps the same order in every case the composed page can be driven through, and is not told apart here. The composition's ask inventory is read where it is not the activation's as well (wzsxvmvw, uowtmmqw). Besides the pointer click on a node's own box and a ref path's activation above, the check parks the view where the centring of the node in hand would change it and requires the viewport to be exactly what it was when `/` opens the field over the canvas, when the active query marks nodes, and when the search's Esc dismisses the field — each case refused when the view it is read from already rests where that centring belongs, so it is never credited to a page that never moves, and each confirmed to have done its own work: the field opens and takes the focus, and the dismissal closes the field and clears the marks and the selection. Those three readings are therefore negative — a page that asks for nothing on those paths reads the same before and after — and they bind exactly a page whose composition asks for a move there: a centring asked on the opening, on the marks a query makes, or on the dismissal is read as the extra ask it is, which neither the activation's ask nor the search's own rule covers, because marking selects nothing and a dismissal names no node either recorded trigger identifies. None of them fixes a member, a message, a duration, an easing or a transform spelling beyond the surface the clauses above already read.
